details:
ORBITAL is an interactive lunar-outpost survival experiment designed to demonstrate the challenges of establishing and maintaining human life on the Moon.

The project places participants in charge of a lunar base for a simulated 30-day mission. They must make decisions and manage interconnected survival systems, including oxygen supply, water, food, electrical power, temperature regulation, radiation protection and habitat safety.

The simulation introduces changing conditions and unexpected mission challenges. Every decision affects other systems, demonstrating the butterfly effect and how a small mistake in one area can create consequences across the entire habitat. Participants must prioritize resources, respond to emergencies and maintain a sustainable environment for the crew.

The experience is designed as an educational, interactive platform that can combine a digital simulation with a physical demonstration using a screen, buttons, LEDs and a microcontroller-based interface.

Its main benefit is making complex space science understandable through hands-on learning. It encourages critical thinking, teamwork, resource management and problem-solving while introducing participants to the engineering challenges of future lunar exploration.

Our creative approach combines game-based learning, realistic mission scenarios, interactive decision-making and immediate feedback. The concept considers scientific accuracy, usability, accessibility, limited resources, energy requirements, environmental conditions and the safety of astronauts.

ORBITAL aims to make space exploration more engaging and help people understand that surviving beyond Earth requires careful planning, interconnected systems and responsible decision-making.
